title: Real-World Multi-Modal and Longitudinal Lung Cancer Dataset (MMIST-LUNG)
authors: Cordeiro Mendes R, Fonseca Verdelho MR, Santiago C, Barata C
type: arXiv preprint v1 (2026-09-04); accepted ECCV 2026 DCA-MI workshop
outcome: 12-month OS (vital_status_12), DSS, dynamic-horizon DSS, discrete hazard
methods: Transformer/mean/max early fusion, late fusion; MLP and XGBoost; 5-fold CV; balanced accuracy
main_result: CLIN 12-month BAcc 56.7 (MLP) / 65.0 (XGB); multimodal more robust when stage removed
relation: EXACT dataset: the benchmark whose labels are audited.
our_critique: Released 12-month labels follow opposite-polarity rules by cohort (CPTAC inverted for recorded deaths); patients without a recorded death are labelled survivors irrespective of follow-up; the CPTAC DSS label is constant. Folds were stratified on these labels. The published numbers were not re-run (original code reads non-released encoded paths); a declared surrogate is used.

title: Auditing Data Leakage and Temporal Misalignment in Machine-Learning Prognosis of Breast Cancer: A Reproducible Censoring-Aware Reanalysis
population: Breast cancer (full text not reviewed in this run)
relation: Closest generic methodological audit, different cancer.
our_critique: Our contribution differs: deterministic source-linked reconstruction of how a released benchmark label was generated (cohort-specific polarity inversion) quantified against upstream GDC records, plus fixed-score paired evaluation. Full text must be read before submission.

title: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks
authors: Northcutt CG, Athalye A, Mueller J
main_result: About 3.3% average test-label error; rankings can flip at realistic error prevalence
our_critique: Their errors are found statistically and confirmed by humans; ours are reconstructed deterministically from code and upstream records in a clinical survival benchmark, are systematic (inverted) rather than random, and are concentrated in one cohort.

title: Label-Space Mismatch Distorts Cross-Cohort Evaluation in Breast Cancer Molecular Subtyping
authors: Liu S, Min B, Zheng Z, Wang J, et al.
main_result: Companion dataset page: TCGA-BRCA accuracy 73.8% to 79.7% under restriction
relation: Label definition distorting cross-cohort evaluation; different task.
our_critique: Adjacent concept, not survival, censoring or polarity. Do not conflate.

title: Harmonizing Public Lung Adenocarcinoma Data for Reproducible Machine Learning
authors: Ahsan MM, Raman S, Siddique Z
main_result: RF AUROC 0.768 at 1 y vs 0.469 at 3 y; eligibility 85 to 46
our_critique: Harmonizes raw TCGA-LUAD fields; does not audit a released multi-cohort benchmark label, CPTAC, or label polarity. Abstract-level review only.

title: The Cost of Binarizing Survival Outcomes in Clinical Prognostic Modeling
authors: Yadav S, Routman DM, Foong AYK
population: Head and neck; breast, colorectal, kidney
main_result: Time-to-event scoring recovers features binarization misses (abstract)
our_critique: Supports the censoring argument; does not address released-label provenance. Abstract only.

title: The Brier Score under Administrative Censoring: Problems and Solutions
main_result: Removing censored individuals biases binary classifiers' apparent performance
our_critique: We apply IPCW at 365 days and add sharp partial-identification bounds; no new method claimed.

title: An Integrated TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource to Drive High-Quality Survival Outcome Analytics (TCGA-CDR)
authors: Liu J, Lichtenberg T, Hoadley KA, et al.
relation: Alternative source release for TCGA (sensitivity analysis).
our_critique: Agrees with GDC on 365-day status for 893/894 jointly ascertainable TCGA patients.

title: Graph Attention-Based Fusion of Pathology Images and Gene Expression for Prediction of Cancer Survival
authors: Zheng Y, Conrad RD, Green EJ, Burks EJ, Betke M, Beane JE, et al.
type: Journal article, IEEE Trans Med Imaging
main_result: TCGA to CPTAC multimodal survival modelling
relation: Shows generic TCGA-to-CPTAC ML is not novel.
our_critique: Our transport design (A2) is a label-evaluation device, not a new model.

title: Clinical usability of an explainable AI decision support tool and evaluation of multimodal models in NSCLC (I3LUNG)
authors: Prelaj A, Miskovic V, et al.
methods: Multimodal models, external validation, usability study
relation: Independent case study for the audit procedure (negative control).
our_critique: OS_6 and OS_24 are fully consistent with the bundle's OS time/event fields and censored-before-horizon cases are left missing. Not external validation of MMIST models.

title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
authors: Collins GS, Moons KGM, Dhiman P, et al.
our_critique: Partly applicable: this study evaluates benchmark labels, not a model for clinical use.
